$schema_doc: Placement constraints for the W25Q16 QSPI flash (U4) and its decoupling cap (C34) vs the RP2040 (U3). Run `python3 hardware/pcb/v2/tools/check_flash_placement.py`. RP2040 datasheet chapter 2.8 recommends flash as close as possible to minimize QSPI trace length at 62MHz default clock.
$boundary_doc: C34 flash Vcc decap uses max_distance_mm=4.68 = centroid-to-pad worst case across 11 RP2040 decaps on the KiCAD_Board_3_Minimal_Full_RP2040 reference board. U4 flash-to-RP2040 chip placement keeps its own 10mm limit (different constraint: QSPI trace length, not bypass). Pass/fail only.

constraints.rationale: Flash chip placed near U3 QSPI_SD0 pin (the most bandwidth-critical signal). RP2040 datasheet 2.8.1: 'The QSPI flash should be placed as close to the chip as possible'. Not a decap — governed by QSPI trace length, not bypass inductance.

Flash Vcc (pin 8) close-in decoupling. W25Q16 datasheet recommends one 100nF per VCC pin at the pin. U4 is SOIC-8 (1.27mm pitch) and the 0402 cap has to sit beyond the lead pad envelope, so ~3mm is the practical minimum; 4.68mm matches the RP2040 reference board's decap centroid-to-pad worst case.
